nodes.label: Researcher / ML engineer
nodes.summary: Configures and submits the training job, watches loss and throughput, and intervenes on rare manual cases (Llama 3 needed manual intervention only three times in 54 days).

nodes.label: Training data
nodes.summary: Tokenized training corpus read by the job. Data curation is outside the sections we read.

nodes.label: Job scheduler (MAST)
nodes.summary: Meta's global-scale training scheduler. Placement is aware of network topology to minimise cross-pod traffic.

nodes.label: GPU cluster
nodes.summary: Up to 16K H100 GPUs for Llama 3 405B (24K in the RoCE cluster), eight per server, 400 Gbps interconnects.

nodes.label: GPU servers
nodes.summary: Grand Teton servers with eight H100 GPUs (80 GB HBM3, 700 W) and two CPUs; GPUs in a server connected by NVLink.

nodes.label: Network fabric (RoCE / InfiniBand)
nodes.summary: RoCE for the 405B model on a three-layer Clos network: 16 GPUs per rack, 3,072-GPU pods with full bisection bandwidth, eight pods with 1:7 oversubscription at the top. Deep-buffer spine switches and E-ECMP with 16 flows per GPU pair.

nodes.label: Collective library (NCCLX)
nodes.summary: A fork of NCCL tuned for high-latency networks; carries FSDP all-gather and reduce-scatter and pipeline point-to-point traffic. Includes tracing and a flight recorder for hangs.

nodes.label: Training job
nodes.summary: One synchronous job spread over thousands of GPUs: a single GPU failure may require a restart of the whole job.

nodes.label: 4D parallelism (TP, CP, PP, FSDP)
nodes.summary: Tensor, context, pipeline and fully sharded data parallelism, ordered by network demand from innermost to outermost. ZeRO-style sharding of optimizer state and gradients reduces memory per GPU.

nodes.label: Checkpointing
nodes.summary: Saves each GPU's state (1 MB to 4 GB) for recovery. MegaScale copies state to host memory in seconds, then writes to the file system in the background; on restore one worker per data-parallel group reads the shared partition.

nodes.label: Distributed file system (Tectonic)
nodes.summary: 240 PB across 7,500 SSD servers, 2 TB/s sustained and 7 TB/s peak throughput. Bursty checkpoint writes saturate it for short periods.

nodes.label: Fault detection and diagnostics
nodes.summary: Heartbeats from every node's daemon, watchdog timeouts, NCCL flight recorder and straggler hunting tools.

nodes.label: Automated recovery
nodes.summary: On a fault, suspends training, runs self-check diagnostics, evicts bad nodes, requests healthy replacements and resumes from the latest checkpoint. MegaScale fixed over 90% of faults automatically.

nodes.label: Alternative: topology-aware job placement only
nodes.summary: Without topology-aware parallelism and scheduling, high-traffic dimensions cross pods and utilisation drops. Llama 3's parallelism plan and scheduler are both aware of the network.

steps.caption: The researcher submits the job; the scheduler picks nodes by network topology.
Batches of tokens stream into the parallel model.
Tensor, context, pipeline and fully sharded data parallel work runs across the GPUs.
Each step exchanges activations, gradients and weights through the collective library.
Traffic crosses the RoCE fabric, with the highest-volume dimensions kept inside servers.
Periodically each GPU's state is checkpointed to the file system.
A node's heartbeat stops or reports an anomaly.
The driver declares a fault and suspends training on all nodes.
Diagnostics find the bad node; it is evicted and a healthy replacement is requested.
Training resumes from the latest checkpoint.
Workers read their state; one worker per data-parallel group reads the shared partition, to avoid overloading storage.

flows.name: A slow GPU drags the whole job (failure mode)

steps.caption: Throughput drops but nothing has failed.
Tools rank the most suspicious communications so engineers (or automation) can find the slow hardware; a single straggler can slow thousands of GPUs.
Thousands of GPUs write at once; the storage fabric saturates briefly.
Two-stage saves (host memory first, then background write) keep GPU pause time short; the aim is a higher checkpoint frequency so less work is lost per recovery.
